formats.title: Chrome Extension manifest.json (Manifest V3)
notes: manifest_version: 3
name: the display name
version: one to four dot-separated integers, e.g. "1.2.0"
background.service_worker: the event-driven background script (replaces MV2 background pages)
action: the toolbar button and its popup (replaces browser_action/page_action)
content_scripts: scripts injected into matching pages
permissions / host_permissions / optional_host_permissions: API and site access
icons / description / options_page / commands
Prefer activeTab over broad host_permissions; it grants access only when the user clicks.
Move site access the extension does not always need into optional_host_permissions and request it at runtime.
Keep service-worker state in chrome.storage; the worker is stopped when idle.
Use declarativeNetRequest instead of blocking webRequest.

formats.title: .NET appsettings.json
notes: None: the file is optional, but Logging and AllowedHosts are in every template
Logging.LogLevel: minimum levels per category ("Default", "Microsoft.AspNetCore")
ConnectionStrings: read with GetConnectionString("Name")
AllowedHosts: host filtering, e.g. "example.com;*.example.com"
Kestrel.Endpoints: listen URLs and certificates
Custom sections: bound to a class with services.Configure<T>(...) or AddOptions<T>().Bind(...)
Later sources win: appsettings.json < appsettings.{Environment}.json < user secrets (Development) < environment variables < command line.
Override nested keys from environment variables with a double underscore: Smtp__Port=2525.
Bind sections to options classes with ValidateOnStart() so bad config fails at boot.

formats.title: GeoJSON FeatureCollection
notes: type: "FeatureCollection" at the root, "Feature" for each feature
features: the array of Feature objects
geometry: per feature, with its own type and coordinates
properties: per feature, an object or null
id: a per-feature identifier
bbox: [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat] bounding box
Coordinates are [longitude, latitude], in that order. Swapping them is the most common GeoJSON bug.
Close polygon rings: the first and last positions must be identical.
Outer rings go counter-clockwise and holes clockwise (the right-hand rule).
Round coordinates to about 6 decimals (roughly 10 cm); more only adds file size.

formats.title: GST e-Invoice JSON (India, IRP schema 1.1)
notes: Version: "1.1"
TranDtls: TaxSch "GST" and SupTyp (B2B, SEZWP, SEZWOP, EXPWP, EXPWOP, DEXP)
DocDtls: Typ (INV, CRN, DBN), No (max 16 chars) and Dt (dd/mm/yyyy)
SellerDtls: Gstin, LglNm, Addr1, Loc, Pin (number), Stcd (state code string)
BuyerDtls: Gstin (or "URP" for exports), LglNm, Pos (place of supply state code), Addr1, Loc, Pin, Stcd
ItemList[]: SlNo, IsServc (Y/N), HsnCd, UnitPrice, TotAmt, AssAmt, GstRt, TotItemVal
ValDtls: AssVal and TotInvVal
TranDtls.RegRev: "Y" for reverse charge; IgstOnIntra: "Y" for IGST on an intra-state supply
ItemList[].Qty / Unit: quantity and UQC unit code (NOS, KGS, OTH...)
ItemList[].IgstAmt or CgstAmt + SgstAmt, CesRt / CesAmt
DispDtls / ShipDtls: dispatch-from and ship-to addresses when they differ
PayDtls, RefDtls, AddlDocDtls, ExpDtls: payment, references, attachments, export details
EwbDtls: transporter and vehicle details to generate the e-way bill with the IRN
Inter-state supply (seller Stcd ≠ buyer Pos) uses IgstAmt; intra-state uses CgstAmt + SgstAmt split equally.
AssAmt = TotAmt − Discount; TotItemVal = AssAmt + taxes + cess + OthChrg. Totals in ValDtls must equal the sum of items (within the IRP rounding tolerance).
Dates are strings in dd/mm/yyyy. Pin codes are numbers; state codes are two-digit strings.
HSN must have at least 4 or 6 digits depending on aggregate turnover; services use SAC codes starting with 99 with IsServc "Y".
Test against the NIC e-invoice sandbox before production; the IRP schema is versioned, so check the current version on the portal.

formats.title: JSON-LD Structured Data (Schema.org Article)
notes: @context: "https://schema.org"
@type: the entity type, e.g. Article, Product, Organization
@graph: several linked entities in one block
@id: a stable URI so entities can reference each other
headline / datePublished / dateModified / author / image: the usual Article properties
publisher: the Organization behind the page
Markup must match what is visible on the page; hidden or invented claims can cost you rich results.
Use ISO 8601 dates with a timezone (2026-11-21T09:00:00+00:00).
Give entities an @id and reference them instead of repeating them.
Test with a rich results testing tool before shipping.

formats.title: JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12)
notes: $schema: the dialect URI, "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"
type: the root type, usually "object"
$id: a unique URI for this schema
properties / required: the fields and which must be present
additionalProperties: false rejects unknown keys
$defs + $ref: reusable sub-schemas ($defs replaced "definitions" in 2019-09)
enum / const / format / pattern / minimum / maxLength: value constraints
oneOf / anyOf / allOf / if-then-else: composition
Always declare $schema so tools pick the right dialect.
Set additionalProperties: false on objects you control; it catches typos.
Use $defs and $ref instead of copy-pasting sub-schemas.
Remember "format" is an annotation by default; turn on format assertion in your validator if you rely on it.

formats.title: LLM Structured Output Request (Claude)
notes: model / max_tokens / messages: the normal Messages API fields
output_config.format.type: "json_schema"
output_config.format.schema: the JSON Schema the reply must match
output_config.effort: low / medium / high / xhigh / max
system: instructions on how to fill each field
tools[].strict: true: the same guarantee for tool-call arguments
Mark every object additionalProperties: false and list required fields.
Describe each field (description) — the model reads them as instructions.
Use nullable types (["string","null"]) for facts that may be missing, rather than letting the model invent them.
Still check stop_reason: a refusal or max_tokens stop can mean there is no complete JSON.

formats.title: package.json (Node.js / npm)
notes: name: lowercase, URL-safe, optionally scoped (@org/name); required to publish
version: a semver string such as "1.2.0"; required to publish
type: "module" makes .js files ESM; omit it (or use "commonjs") for CommonJS
exports: the public entry points; anything not listed cannot be imported
scripts: commands run with npm run <name>
engines: the supported Node.js range
dependencies / devDependencies / peerDependencies: runtime, build-time and host-provided packages
files: allow-list of what gets published
private: true blocks accidental npm publish
Use an "exports" map instead of "main" alone; it also hides internal files.
Put the "types" condition first inside each exports entry.
Keep build tools (typescript, vitest, eslint) in devDependencies.
Commit the lockfile, and set "private": true on apps that are never published.

formats.title: Power BI Report Theme JSON
notes: name: the theme name shown in Power BI
dataColors: array of hex colors used for series, in order
firstLevelElements / secondLevelElements / thirdLevelElements / fourthLevelElements: text and line colors from primary to subtle
background / secondaryBackground: canvas and visual backgrounds
tableAccent: grid and header accent in tables and matrices
good / neutral / bad: KPI and sentiment colors
maximum / center / minimum / null: diverging and conditional-formatting colors
textClasses: callout, title, header and label font size, family and color
visualStyles: default formatting per visual type ("*" = all visuals) and per style ("*" = all)
Give dataColors at least 8 colors; Power BI cycles through them for extra series.
Use textClasses for fonts instead of setting fonts in visualStyles one by one.
Start visualStyles with "*" / "*" for global defaults, then override specific visuals like "card".
Check contrast: first-level text on background should meet WCAG AA (4.5:1).
Use a JSON Schema-aware editor with Microsoft's published report theme schema to catch misspelled properties, which Power BI silently ignores.

formats.title: Sample REST API JSON Response (Paginated)
notes: data: the array of records (an empty array, not null, when there are no results)
meta.pagination: page, perPage, total, totalPages (offset style) or nextCursor (cursor style)
links: self / next / prev URLs so clients do not build them by hand
errors: array of { code, message, field } objects; empty on success
meta.requestId: correlates the response with server logs
Return [] for no results, never null; clients can always iterate.
Prefer cursor pagination for large or fast-changing tables; page numbers skip or repeat rows when data shifts.
Use the same envelope on every endpoint so clients can share one parser.
Use ISO 8601 UTC timestamps and string ids (64-bit numeric ids lose precision in JavaScript).
Put the HTTP status in the status line; do not repeat it as a "success": true field.

formats.title: Sample JSON Data (Employees, Students, Products)
notes: A top-level object or array: valid JSON must have exactly one root value
Double-quoted keys and strings: single quotes are not valid JSON
employees: array of objects with id, name, email, department, salary, isActive, manager (null for top-level), skills (array), address (nested object)
departments: lookup array referenced by employees[].department
students: array with grades (object of subject → score) and enrolledAt (ISO 8601 date)
products: array with price (number), tags (array) and variants (array of objects)
Keep ids unique and stable so related records (manager, department) can reference them.
Store dates as ISO 8601 strings ("2024-03-15" or "2024-03-15T09:30:00Z"); JSON has no date type.
Store money as a number of the smallest unit or as a number plus a currency field; never mix formats.
Use null for "known to be empty" and omit the key for "not applicable".
Use example.com / example.org email domains so test data can never reach a real inbox.

formats.title: tsconfig.json (TypeScript)
notes: compilerOptions: the compiler settings (an empty tsconfig still works on defaults, but you rarely want them)
include / exclude / files: which sources are in the project
extends: inherit from a shared base such as @tsconfig/node22
references: project references for monorepos (with composite: true)
compilerOptions.paths: import aliases
Turn on "strict": true from day one; retrofitting it later is painful.
For Node, pair "module": "nodenext" with "moduleResolution": "nodenext"; for Vite/webpack apps use "module": "esnext" with "moduleResolution": "bundler".
Add "noUncheckedIndexedAccess" to catch undefined array and record lookups.
Use "verbatimModuleSyntax" so type-only imports are explicit and erased predictably.

formats.title: Zoom Rooms Controls profile for Q-SYS
notes: adapters — one entry per control endpoint; for Q-SYS use model "GenericNetworkAdapter"
adapters[].ip — "tcp://<core-ip>:1702" (the Q-SYS ECP port; private IPs only)
adapters[].ports[] — the device: unique id, name and its methods
ports[].methods[] — id, name, command, type ("action" or "actions" with params)
methods[].params — choices substituted for % in command (e.g. 1/0 for mute)
styles — main button, names and icons, e.g. "qsys_core.main_method=mute"
rules — Zoom events → device commands: meeting_started, meeting_ended, microphone_muted, microphone_unmuted, video_started, video_stopped, operation_time_started, operation_time_ended
Export every control the profile uses as a Named Control in Q-SYS Designer — ECP addresses controls by that exact, case-sensitive name.
End each ECP command with \n (LF). A \r before it is ignored, so \r\n also works.
Use % in command plus params for on/off or up/down variants instead of duplicating methods.
Keep model exactly "GenericNetworkAdapter" — Zoom only accepts iTachIP2SL, iTachIP2CC and GenericNetworkAdapter.
Test commands with a telnet session to the Core on port 1702 before pasting the profile into Zoom.
